observation_summary: The compiler fails to issue a warning for useless code when the side-effect-free expression is not the first element in a comma-separated sequence.
reasoning_summary: The bug occurs because the side-effect checker only evaluates the first element of a comma-separated expression sequence. As described in the bug report and confirmed by the failing test cases, non-rightmost elements in a comma expression are ignored during the side-effect analysis. Consequently, expressions that contain side-effect-free code in positions other than the first are not flagged as problematic, leading to the failure of the assertion that expects a warning for useless code.
